proposal.summary: Teleport 9.3.6 contains a command injection vulnerability in handling an ssh-agent installation link where a URL‑encoded bash escape with CRLF can be used as a token to execute commands, enabling unauthenticated remote code execution via social engineering.
proposal.cwe_quote: An attacker can craft a malicious ssh agent installation link by URL encoding a bash escape with carriage return line feed.

AV.quote: This is fully unauthenticated attack utilizing the trusted teleport server to deliver the payload.

PR.quote: This is fully unauthenticated attack utilizing the trusted teleport server to deliver the payload.

UI.quote: This url encoded payload can be used in place of a token and sent to a user in a social engineering attack.

C.quote: Teleport 9.3.6 is vulnerable to Command injection leading to Remote Code Execution.

I.quote: Teleport 9.3.6 is vulnerable to Command injection leading to Remote Code Execution.

A.quote: Teleport 9.3.6 is vulnerable to Command injection leading to Remote Code Execution.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Obtain a proof-of-concept or reproduction steps and immediately notify the Teleport product security team; if confirmed, coordinate disclosure and provide mitigations such as blocking crafted tokens and updating to a patched release.
